cards.title: Mary Hill Garden

cards.title: Duke Student Commons

cards.evidence_claim: The turtle pond in Wynn Amphitheater is a favorite spot for students to observe animals and relax.

cards.title: The Mother Road Tribute
cards.subtitle: Foothill Boulevard Corridor
cards.notes: Stop by the corner of Foothill and Alameda to see the 'Greetings from Azusa' mural, celebrating the city's identity as a Route 66 gateway.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale public mural and monument commemorating Azusa's history on the historic Mother Road.
cards.evidence_claim: A Route 66 mural and Centennial Monument are located at the corner of Foothill Blvd and Alameda, adjacent to City Hall.
cards.source_title: Azusa, CA - Route 66 Centennial Monument Project
cards.access_notes: Public art installation visible from the sidewalk 24/7.

cards.title: The Nature Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Citrus Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk north on Citrus Avenue to reach this 11-acre park, offering walking trails and a peaceful alternative to campus lawns for studying.
cards.short_summary: A quiet municipal park north of campus used by students for recreation and outdoor study.
cards.evidence_claim: Northside Park is a great spot for students to enjoy walking trails and a peaceful atmosphere for study sessions.
cards.source_title: Free and Affordable Activities for College Students at APU
cards.access_notes: Public park; open daily from dawn to dusk.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Rooted in its Wesleyan heritage and 'God First' motto, Azusa Pacific University maintains a unique culture of spiritual formation, community service, and seasonal celebrations that define the Cougar experience.

cards.title: The Chapel Rhythm
cards.subtitle: A communal pause for worship
cards.notes: Attend one of the six weekly chapel options to experience corporate worship. It is a cornerstone of student life, offering a built-in break for spiritual rest and peer connection.
cards.short_summary: A central campus tradition where students gather multiple times a week for worship, testimonies, and spiritual formation.
cards.evidence_claim: Chapel is a campus-wide tradition held several times a week, hosted on both campuses to cultivate disciples and scholars through corporate worship.
cards.source_title: Why Chapel? - APU Articles - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Held Monday, Wednesday, and Friday mornings; Senior Chapel occurs Monday nights.

cards.title: Midnight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: The ultimate finals week study break
cards.notes: Head to the dining hall late at night during finals week for a festive breakfast served by faculty and staff. It is a high-energy tradition to fuel late-night study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A late-night communal meal served during finals week to provide students with a much-needed break and encouragement.
cards.evidence_claim: Midnight Breakfast is listed as a 'must-do' tradition before graduation, typically held as a study break during final exams.
cards.source_title: 50 Things to Do Before Graduation | APU Student Bucket List - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Occurs late at night during finals week each semester.

cards.title: Common Day of Learning
cards.subtitle: A festival of academic discovery
cards.notes: Participate in this day-long conference where classes are replaced by scholarly seminars. It is a unique opportunity to see faculty and students present original research together.
cards.short_summary: An annual multidisciplinary conference dedicated to the celebration of academic discovery and scholarly exchange across the university.
cards.evidence_claim: The Common Day of Learning is a campus-wide multidisciplinary conference featuring scholarly seminars with faculty and students.
cards.source_title: APU Presents 23rd Annual Common Day of Learning - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Annual event held in the spring semester; open to the public.

cards.title: The Dinner Rally
cards.subtitle: A legacy of investment
cards.notes: Attend this formal gala to support student scholarships. This decades-old tradition features world-class musical performances by students and stories of university impact.
cards.short_summary: APU's longest-running fundraising tradition, bringing the community together for over 70 years to support student financial aid.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dinner Rally is an annual fundraising gala held for over 72 years to raise money for student scholarships through performances and speakers.
cards.source_title: Dinner Rally: A Legacy of Investment - ZU Media
cards.access_notes: Annual event typically held in October; requires registration.

cards.title: Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: A winter wonderland in Azusa
cards.notes: Join the community for the annual lighting of the campus tree. The event features carols, festive treats, and a transformation of the plaza into a holiday celebration.
cards.short_summary: A beloved seasonal tradition where students and locals gather to kick off the Advent season with music and lights.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual tree lighting is a beloved APU tradition that transforms West Campus into a winter wonderland for students and the community.
cards.source_title: APU Christmas Tree Lighting | Advent 2024 - YouTube
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December.

cards.title: Night of Champions
cards.subtitle: Inspiration and perspiration
cards.notes: Volunteer or attend this massive outreach event featuring Olympic athletes and celebrities. It combines high-energy games with powerful faith-based testimonies.
cards.short_summary: A signature youth outreach event hosted by APU for over 35 years, featuring sports, food, and inspirational speakers.
cards.evidence_claim: Night of Champions is a signature APU event that has run for over 35 years, drawing thousands of youth to hear from world-class athletes and artists.
cards.source_title: APU Hosts 37th Night of Champions - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Annual event typically held in November; tickets required for participants.

cards.title: The Service Requirement
cards.subtitle: Scholarship put into practice
cards.notes: Complete your required service credits by engaging with local non-profits or global missions. It is a graduation requirement that reflects the university's commitment to service.
cards.short_summary: A mandatory tradition of community engagement where every undergraduate student completes service hours to graduate.
cards.evidence_claim: Service is one of APU's Four Cornerstones, and all full-time undergraduate students must complete a specific number of service credits to graduate.
cards.source_title: Service Requirement - OSD
cards.access_notes: Ongoing requirement throughout a student's tenure at APU.

cards.title: Candela
cards.subtitle: A symbolic commissioning
cards.notes: Participate in this candle-lighting ceremony during Welcome Weekend. It marks the beginning of your journey as a 'difference maker' in the APU community.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic commissioning ceremony for new students and their families to mark the start of their university experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Candela is a symbolic time of commissioning and blessing held during the Fall Welcome Weekend for the APU community.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Held annually on the Friday night of Welcome Weekend.

cards.title: Global Engagement Trips
cards.subtitle: Serving the world
cards.notes: Join a GE team to serve internationally during spring or summer breaks. These trips are a long-standing tradition of intercultural learning and ministry.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of short-term mission and service trips where students travel globally to live out the university's mission.
cards.evidence_claim: Global Engagement teams provide opportunities for students to serve nationally and internationally, earning 30 service credits per experience.
cards.source_title: Global Engagement - OSD
cards.access_notes: Trips occur during fall, spring, and summer breaks; application required.

cards.title: The Cougar Walk
cards.subtitle: The heart of East Campus
cards.notes: Walk the central pedestrian artery of East Campus. It is the site of club fairs, spontaneous worship, and the primary path connecting student life buildings.
cards.short_summary: The main thoroughfare of East Campus that serves as the social and spiritual hub for the student body.
cards.evidence_claim: Cougar Walk is described as being in the heart of APU's East Campus, overlooked by the Upper Turner Campus Center and serving as a place for student gathering.
cards.source_title: Sacred Encounters Throughout APU's History - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a campus thoroughfare.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Azusa Pacific University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential traditions, campus landmarks, and student rituals that define the first weekend for new Cougars at Azusa Pacific University.

cards.title: Check In at Bode Commons
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Start your journey by picking up your Welcome Weekend t-shirt, meal wristband, and Alpha Group assignment at this central East Campus hub.
cards.short_summary: The official starting point for new students to collect orientation materials and schedules.
cards.evidence_claim: Welcome Weekend check-in begins at 8:30 a.m. on Friday at Bode Commons, where students receive t-shirts and group assignments.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Check-in typically runs from 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. on the first Friday of Welcome Weekend.

cards.title: Ride the Campus Trolley
cards.subtitle: Inter-Campus Transit
cards.notes: Hop on the iconic red, blue, or green trolleys to travel between East and West campuses; it is a staple of the APU student experience.
cards.short_summary: A themed shuttle service connecting the two main sections of the Azusa campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The trolley system is a campus staple that shuttles students between East and West campuses with continuous service during the day.
cards.source_title: APU Transportation Services | Campus Shuttles and Van Rentals - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Trolleys operate until 7:00 p.m. on Fridays and have special hours during Welcome Weekend.

cards.title: Explore the Community Fair
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Connection
cards.notes: Walk this central East Campus pathway to meet local business representatives and campus departments during the orientation resource fair.
cards.short_summary: A central campus thoroughfare that hosts the community resource fair during Welcome Weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The community fair is held on Cougar Walk on East Campus, featuring representatives from APU departments and local businesses.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Open to all students during the scheduled fair hours, typically 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

cards.title: Enjoy Root Beer Floats
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Tradition
cards.notes: Join a long-standing tradition by grabbing a free root beer float and a commemorative APU mug hosted by Alumni Engagement.
cards.short_summary: A traditional social event where new students receive a university mug and a treat.
cards.evidence_claim: The root beer float tradition is hosted by Alumni Engagement at the Dillon Recreation Complex during Welcome Weekend.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Typically held on Friday afternoon; check the official schedule for exact timing.

cards.title: Watch the 'Good Times' Show
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Entertainment
cards.notes: Bring a blanket to the lawn for this traditional talent showcase featuring Alpha Leaders and student performers.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor evening performance that is a staple of the first weekend experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Good Times is a traditional favorite event held at the Dillon Recreation Complex from 7:30-9:00 p.m. on Friday.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event; students are encouraged to arrive early for seating on the lawn.

cards.title: Refuel at Cornerstone
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Study Spot
cards.notes: Located next to Marshburn Library, this is the go-to spot for Peet's Coffee and the signature 'blended Naked' smoothie.
cards.short_summary: The primary coffee shop on East Campus, popular for both socializing and studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Cornerstone Coffeehouse is located on East Campus adjacent to the Marshburn Memorial Library and serves Peet's Coffee.
cards.source_title: Top Coffee Shops Near Azusa Pacific University Students Love
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; accepts dining dollars and Cougar Bucks.

cards.title: Relax by the Turtle Pond
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Break
cards.notes: Take a quiet moment at the Wynn Amphitheater turtle pond, a favorite campus spot for observing wildlife and finding peace.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil outdoor area on East Campus known for its resident turtles.
cards.evidence_claim: The turtle pond in Wynn Amphitheater is cited as a favorite campus spot for students to relax and observe animals.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible 24/7 as an outdoor campus space.

cards.title: Gather for Welcome Worship
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Session
cards.notes: Experience the energy of the APU community with a time of worship and a special blessing in this massive West Campus arena.
cards.short_summary: The primary venue for large-scale university gatherings, including orientation worship services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Felix Event Center on West Campus hosts university events such as chapel and orientation worship sessions.
cards.source_title: Fall Welcome Weekend Schedule - Azusa Pacific University
cards.access_notes: Check-in for late arrivals also moves to the Felix Event Center ticket window after 5:00 p.m. on Friday.

cards.title: Visit the Prayer Garden
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Reflection
cards.notes: Find tranquility among the trees and stones in this garden located between the Felix Event Center and the Mary Hill Building.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful outdoor space on West Campus designed for prayer and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mary Hill garden is a prayer garden located between the Felix Event Center and the Mary Hill Building on West Campus.
cards.source_title: APU Students' and Alumni's Favorite Spots On Campus
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space accessible to all students.

cards.title: Meet at Duke Commons
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Social
cards.notes: Wrap up your weekend by socializing or grabbing a meal at this West Campus hub, which also houses the One Card Office.
cards.short_summary: A modern student center on West Campus for dining, studying, and administrative services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Duke Student Commons serves as a welcoming space for all APU students for dining and socializing on West Campus.
cards.source_title: In This Space: Students Feel at Home in the Duke Student Commons
cards.access_notes: Home to the One Card Office for ID card issues during orientation.
